Textiles and Leather V. 26.1 2/9

1. Implementation

The document has been created and approved by the General Assembly of 09.11.2024.
The document and its rules have been implemented since the 2025 season.

2. Definition

2.1. Importance of Aesthetics

Armors and weapons aesthetics are very important for the fighters' appearance and _ sports
representation. The development of our sport will be easier with well-maintained and properly finished
armor and weapons.

2.2. Textiles and leather

Textiles and leather are part of a knightly appearance. Tabards are made of fabric (linen, wool, silk...),
coats of plates are covered with fabric, leather is mainly used for armor (helmet suspension, belts,
pouches, straps), etc.

All skin of a competitor must be covered.

3. General Requirements

Textiles and Leather must:

● be based on historical sources,

● not be of a clearly modern color (I.E neon or fluorescent),

● be maintained in a good shape prior to any Buhurt International Event,
● not be decorated with modern images, offensive logos, etc.

4. Textiles

4.1. Historical Sources and Datation

The sources provide the following available materials during the Middle Ages:

● linen,
● wool,
● silk,

● coton.

Those materials are Approved for 14th century, Transitional and 15th century armors.

Depending on the area and time-period, other textiles fibers may be available. Any other material based
on historical sources can be accepted.

Textiles were used in many applications, such as:

● tabard,

● covering a coat of plates, corazzina or brigandine,
● gambesons,

● chausses,

● helmet decoration (burlet, torse, orle, crest etc.).

4.2. Specific Requirements
Any material listed in 4.1 is Approved.
Any material based on historical sources thus not listed in 4.1 is Approved.
It is Approved to use a modern material under the following conditions:

● the modern material replicates the aesthetic of an approved material listed in 4.1,
● the modern material is strong enough to endure full contact fights and to not be damaged too
easily.
We recommend asking for approval of the Authenticity Committee regarding modern materials before
placing an order for an item made of such material.

Any clearly modern cloth element, such as underpants, sport legging, knee pad etc., must not be visible
from any position.

5. Leather

5.1. Historical Sources and Datation

The sources provide a numerous amount of information about the use of leather. Leather can be
decorated or not.

The use of leather is Approved for 14th century, Transitional and 15th century armors.
Leather was used in many applications, such as:

● covering a coat of plates, corazzina or brigandine,
● gambesons,

● helmet element (suspension system, straps etc.),
● belts,

● pouches,

● shoes,

● etc.

5.2. Specific Requirements

Any natural leather is Approved.
It is Approved to use a modern material under the following conditions:

● the modern material replicates the aesthetic of an approved material listed in 4.1,
● the modern material is strong enough to endure full contact fights and to not be damaged too
easily.
We recommend asking for approval of the Authenticity Committee regarding modern materials before
placing an order for an item made of such material.

Specific Requirements for boots and shoes
Boots and shoes must:

● be based on historical sources,
● be fastened by leather laces, fabric laces or any historically plausible mechanism,
● have a flat sole made of leather, or modern material.

Modern rubber soles must be flat or with very low texture.
It is Denied to use rubber sole to mimic hiking boots sole
Modern soles must be black or brown, with no modern flashing color.
